metadata.title: 7 करोड़ आदिवासियों की स्क्रीनिंग आख़िर क्यों | Why 70 million tribals need to be screened ?
metadata.description: Sickle cell anemia is a prevalent disease among tribal populations in India, affecting a significant portion of this demographic. The Indian government has set an ambitious goal to eradicate sickle cell anaemia from the country by 2047 and has announced a special program to achieve this target. However, this initiative faces several challenges, the most significant being the need to screen at least 7 crore (70 million) people for the disease. There is also a concern that tribal individuals found to have this condition may face social isolation within society. Achieving this goal will require a comprehensive and inclusive approach that addresses healthcare access, education, and social stigma associated with sickle cell anaemia among tribal communities.
